summary: Five-row paged text list: fills the five row panes of one page from the total row count at +0x4C and the rows-on-this-page count at +0x50, moves the selection through the embedded row table at +0x54 and notifies its owner through vtable +0x6C. Same 436-byte layout as Ui_TextListWindow.
evidence: vtable 0x00771BE4 (slot 14 = Ui_PageList_ShowPage 0x0045F09C, slots 12/13 = StepSelectionUp/Down 0x002CF878/0x002CF838). ShowPage loops i<5 over rows at 0x70 (stride 0xC: paneA +0, paneB +4, row id +8), reads rowCount at +0x4C, computes the page row count into +0x50 (reciprocal multiply by 5) and calls Ui_List_SelectEntryById(self->f_38, (rows-1) | u16(+0x28)<<16). StepSelectionUp/Down call Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects(self+0x54) (asm: add r0,r0,#0x54) and then the owner slot +0x6C with self->f_64.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Vtable 0x00771BE4 installed by the class constructor; 15 slots, slot 12/13 step the selection and slot 14 is Ui_PageList_ShowPage.

fields.name: maybe_paneGroupId
fields.evidence: u16 shifted into the high 16 bits of every pane/entry id: Ui_List_SelectEntryById(list, (pageRows-1) | *(u16*)(self+0x28)<<16) in ShowPage. Same field is set from the widget init argument drN (0x001A6520) 5th parameter and is used the same way by Ui_TextListWindow/Ui_TwoColumnList; the exact meaning (text layer/group id) is not proven.

fields.name: entryList
fields.evidence: ShowPage reads *(int*)(self+0x38) as the Ui_List to select into: its +0xC is the current entry id, compared with the page row count, and it is passed as self to Ui_List_SelectEntryById. Ui_Object_DtorBase also releases a sub-object at +0x38 through vtable+4.

fields.name: rowCount
fields.evidence: ShowPage: idx = page*5+i; if ((int)idx < *(int*)(self+0x4C)) the row is filled from that entry, else the row is blanked and its id set to 0xFF. This is the total number of rows across all pages.

fields.name: pageRowCount
fields.evidence: ShowPage sets self->f_50 = 5 first, then recomputes it as (rowCount - page*5) modulo 5 (magic divide by 5) and compares it with the list's current entry id; it is the number of rows shown on the current page.

fields.name: rowTable
fields.evidence: First word (vtable) of the embedded row table built by the tiny ctor 0x00622248 (vtable 0x00780224): two text panes at +4/+8, current index at +0x10, row-descriptor array at +0x1C (= self+0x70, {paneA, paneB, rowId} stride 0xC, written by ShowPage). Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects(self+0x54, dir) steps its index (asm add r0,r0,#0x54).

fields.name: currentRowIndex
fields.evidence: StepSelectionUp/Down load [self+0x64] (asm ldr r1,[r4,#0x64]) and forward it to the owner's vtable slot +0x6C right after Ui_TextListWindow_StepItemRects(self+0x54) changed it; it is the rowTable's +0x10 index field.

fields.name: unknown_0x1b0
fields.evidence: No real access: struct_db derived 0x1B0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x6C from the line '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x6c))(param_1,param_1[0x19])'. The only real fields touched there are the vtable and +0x64.

summary: Five-row selection list ('select1'..'select5'): builds one row per set game-work flag (five flags read through 0x00629FB8 from the bag work), stores the chosen source row ids in a six-byte array at +0x1DC, labels the rows through 'select%d' pane names and keeps the selectable entry table at +0x1E4.
evidence: InitPanes 0x002B7440 formats 'select%d' names, binds five 0x50-byte Ui_AnimRef rows starting at +0x4C with Ui_AnimRef_Bind(row, self->f_4, name, 0) and hides panes 5..9; BuildRows 0x002B7000 clears six row ids at +0x1DC to 0xFF, tests five flags with FUN_00629FB8(work+0x24A98, i), checks the entry table at self->f_1E4 (count at +0x60, array at +0x58), re-binds the rows and resizes the list through vtable +0x2C/+0x3C.

fields.name: layout
fields.evidence: InitPanes loads self->f_4 into iVar4 and passes it as the second (layout) argument of Ui_AnimRef_Bind for every row: FUN_003E00CC(self+0x4C+i*0x50, iVar4, 'select%d', 0); Ui_AnimRef_Bind uses that argument to look up the pane and stores it back into the anim object.

fields.evidence: No real access: 0xB0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x2C from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x2c))(param_1)' in BuildRows. The class layout has five 0x50-byte rows at 0x4C, so 0xB0 falls inside row 1 and is not a distinct field.

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0xD0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x34 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))(param_1,puVar3,uVar6 | ...,0)' (set-cell slot) in InitPanes.

fields.name: unknown_0xe0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0xE0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x38 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x38))' (set-cell-row slot) in InitPanes.

summary: Row/column grid table: clamps the requested row and column counts to at least 1, stores them as u8 at +0xD/+0xE and allocates the 0x34-byte row-record and 0x2C-byte column-record arrays whose pointers live at +0x94/+0x98.
evidence: AllocRows 0x003BEEB8 takes the counts from a parameter block (+0x12 rows, +0x14 columns, both u16), clamps each to >=1, writes them at self+0xD/self+0xE, allocates rows*0x34+8 and columns*0x2C+8 bytes with Mem_AllocAligned 0x0010F6EC (each block headed by [elementSize, count]) and default-constructs them with std_ConstructArray 0x00100050, then clears the two array pointers at self+0x94/self+0x98.

fields.name: rowCount
fields.evidence: uVar3 = MAX(*(u16*)(params+0x12), 1); *(u8*)(self+0xD) = uVar3; the same count sizes the 0x34-byte row-record array.

fields.name: columnCount
fields.evidence: *(u8*)(self+0xE) = MAX(*(u16*)(params+0x14), 1); read back (uVar3 = *(u8*)(self+0xE)) to size the 0x2C-byte column-record array.

fields.name: rows
fields.evidence: After allocating the rowCount*0x34 record block, AllocRows clears *(u32*)(self+0x94); Ghidra dropped the real pointer store after the noreturn-marked std_ConstructArray, but the allocation shape (0x34-byte records, count at +0xD) makes this the row array pointer.

fields.name: columns
fields.evidence: Second allocation of columnCount*0x2C records; *(u32*)(self+0x98) is cleared right after it (same dropped-store pattern), so this is the column-record array pointer.

summary: Scrolling page list: keeps the page/scroll index at +0x4C and the cursor list at +0x38; ScrollToIndex/ScrollToTop/ScrollBy move the index, re-select the visible entry through Ui_List_SelectEntryById and refresh the window through vtable +0x60.
evidence: ScrollToIndex 0x006E57E4: vtable+0x64 is the entry count, page = index/12 (reciprocal multiply, magic DAT_006e58fc), FUN_001D809C(list at self[0xE], rowInPage + index - 12*page | u16(self+0x28)<<16), self[0x13] = page, then vtable+0x60. ScrollToTop 0x006E5900 sets self[0x13]=0 and reselects. ScrollBy 0x006E59C4 adds the delta to self[0x13] and wraps it into [0, pages-1] using vtable+0x64. Callers are equipment/shop/smith list windows.

fields.name: entryList
fields.evidence: param_1[0xe] (self+0x38) is checked for null and passed as the list to Ui_List_SelectEntryById together with the new entry id; its +0xC is the currently selected entry id, exactly like Ui_PageList's list at +0x38.

fields.name: pageIndex
fields.evidence: param_1[0x13]. ScrollToTop sets it to 0; ScrollToIndex sets it to the page computed from the target index (index/12, 12 rows per page); ScrollBy adds the delta and wraps it into [0, (entryCount-1)/N-1] using vtable+0x64; MoveCursorWithPage does the same.

fields.name: unknown_0x180
fields.evidence: No real access: 0x180 = 4 * vtable slot 0x60 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x60))(param_1)' (refresh slot) in ScrollToIndex/ScrollToTop/ScrollByAnimated.

fields.name: unknown_0x1a0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0x1A0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x68 from 'iVar5 = (**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x68))(param_1)' (row-in-page getter) in ScrollToIndex/ScrollToTop.

summary: Battle damage-popup group (the same object the project already calls Ui_DamagePopupGroup, vtable 0x00778A90): owns six 0x50-byte 'pop_damage1'..'pop_damage6' sub-windows starting at +0x4C; each popup keeps its layout pane at +4 and its number-part handle at +0x4C. The 'seven' in the generated name counts the base object plus six popups.
evidence: Ctor 0x004CF348 chains Ui_Object_CtorBase 0x001A66A0 and builds six 0x50-byte sub-objects at 0x4C, 0x9C, 0xEC, 0x13C, 0x18C, 0x1DC (vtable DAT_004cf3b4, record pointer cleared); dtor 0x004CF3BC/0x004CF408 destroys them in reverse with Ui_Object_DtorBase 0x001A6768. Ui_DamagePopupGroup_Init 0x004CEFC0 (vtable slot 8) proves the purpose: 'add fp,sl,#0x4c' then for 'pop_damage1'..'pop_damage6' drN(group+0x4C+i*0x50, pane, ..) and Ui_PlayAnimByName(*(u32*)(group+0x4C+i*0x50+4), ...) stores the number part at group+0x4C+i*0x50+0x4C (0x98, 0xE8, 0x138, 0x188, 0x1D8, 0x228). Size 0x22C = 0x4C + 6*0x50 (structs.json's own Ui_DamagePopupGroup is 556 bytes); the batch's 480 only reached the last popup start.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x004CF348 stores DAT_004cf3b0 (vtable 0x00778A90, slot 8 = Ui_DamagePopupGroup_Init 0x004CEFC0) at self[0]; the two dtors install DAT_004cf3b4/0x004cf3b0 variants.

fields.name: damagePopup1
fields.evidence: First of six embedded 0x50-byte popup sub-windows: Ui_DamagePopupGroup_Init does 'add fp,sl,#0x4c' and calls drN(group+0x4C, 'pop_damage1' pane, ..); its number-part handle is stored at group+0x98 (= popup+0x4C).

fields.name: damagePopup1Pane
fields.evidence: *(u32*)(group+0x50) = popup1+0x4 = the 'pop_damage1' layout pane found by the layout virtual +0x2C; Ui_DamagePopupGroup_Init passes it to Ui_PlayAnimByName(...,DAT_004cf308,0,1) and stores the returned number-part object at +0x98.

fields.name: damagePopup6
fields.evidence: Sixth (last) 0x50-byte popup at 0x4C + 5*0x50 = 0x1DC: Ui_DamagePopupGroup_Init calls drN(group+0x1DC, 'pop_damage6' pane, ..) and stores its number part at group+0x228 (= popup6+0x4C); dtor 0x004CF3BC destroys it first (FUN_001A6768(param_1 + 0x77) = +0x1DC).

summary: Small text-measure record: a pending-measure flag at +0 and a wide string at +0x1C that the update method re-measures with wcslen; the class name was recovered from function names, but struct_db mixed the 0x10-byte ctor of this small record with the measure-update code of a larger text object, so the high offsets in the batch are not distinct fields.
evidence: CtorSmall 0x004A5D60 zeroes a 0x10-byte record (u32 at +0, four bytes at +4..+7, std_ConstructArray(self+8, 2, 3)); ClearRows 0x004A5E38 uses the widget base ctor drN and writes 7 rows through vtable +0x38; UpdateMeasureState 0x001B827C is declared 'char* self' and uses the byte at +0 as a pending flag, the byte at +0x2C as its result flag and wcslen(0x00100B74) on self+0x1C. Only the +0 flag is a real field of the batch's offsets.

fields.name: maybe_measurePending
fields.evidence: UpdateMeasureState: 'if (*param_1 == 1)' starts the async measure; the flag is cleared ('*param_1 = 0') before re-measuring, and CtorSmall zeroes it. A pending/queued state flag rather than a vtable (no vtable store and no virtual call in the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_0x70
fields.evidence: No real field: 0x70 = 4 * the real byte offset 0x1C from 'FUN_00100b74(param_1 + 0x1c)' (wcslen on the wide string) because UpdateMeasureState's param_1 is char*, not int*.

fields.name: unknown_0xb0
fields.evidence: No real field: 0xB0 = 4 * the real byte offset 0x2C from 'param_1[0x2c] = cVar1' (the measure-result flag) in UpdateMeasureState, again a char* element access.

fields.name: unknown_0xe0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0xE0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x38 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x38))' (set-row slot) in ClearRows.

summary: Bag/equipment list: maps the selected row to the equipped item of the party member recorded at +0x49 through the six-slot list at +0x38, and computes each row's state from a flag byte table in the save work (bag work +0x5A4E) indexed by the base at +0x298.
evidence: GetRowState 0x0064C7E0 returns 0 for state bytes 0x01/0x04 and 3 otherwise, reading *(char*)(work+0x2A4E6 + *(u16*)(self+0x298) + rowId) where work comes from Game_GetWork and +0x2A4E6 = bag work (+0x24A98) + 0x5A4E. GetSelectedItemId 0x0064C408: member = Party_Member record 0x0035EB98(work, *(u8*)(self+0x49)) for memberIndex < 0x1F, then slot = *(u16*)(*(int*)(self+0x38)+0xC) for slot < 6 and returns Ui_Member_GetEquippedItemId 0x006292F0(member, slot). SetLabel 0x0064DF88 uses Party_GetActiveMemberCount 0x0063A8A0.

fields.name: entryList
fields.evidence: GetSelectedItemId: uVar3 = *(u16*)(*(int*)(self+0x38)+0xC) (current entry id of the list at +0x38); only slots 0..5 are valid, matching the six equipment slots of a PartyMember, and the result is passed to Ui_Member_GetEquippedItemId.

fields.name: memberIndex
fields.evidence: GetSelectedItemId: if (*(u8*)(self+0x49) < 0x1F) FUN_0035EB98(work, *(u8*)(self+0x49)) - party member records are 31 entries of 0x12EC bytes, so this is the list's current party-member row (0..30).

fields.name: maybe_rowTableBase
fields.evidence: GetRowState indexes the save-work byte table at bag+0x5A4E with (u16)(self+0x298) + rowId and uses the byte (1/4 => state 0, else 3) as the row state. A page/tab base offset into that table; the exact table meaning is not proven, hence maybe_.

summary: Six-row command list window with a 'txt_title' heading: fills six rows from the 9-entry command-id table at 0x00479B38. Only the row builder was recovered and it touches the widget purely through its vtable, so none of the batch's offsets is a real field of its own.
evidence: BuildRows 0x004799CC starts with the widget base ctor drN 0x001A6520, sets the 'txt_title' pane through vtable +0x34, then for i<6 reads a command id from the byte table at 0x00479B38 (only when i<9), resolves it with 0x00633560 and writes the row through vtable +0x34 with id ((u16)(self+0x28)<<16 | 1) + i, and finally refreshes through vtable +0x48.

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0xD0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x34 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))' (set-text slot) in BuildRows.

fields.name: unknown_0xe0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0xE0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x38 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x38))' (set-row slot) in BuildRows.

fields.name: unknown_0x120
fields.evidence: No real access: 0x120 = 4 * vtable slot 0x48 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x48))(param_1, ...)' (refresh slot) in BuildRows.

summary: Party roster window: an eight-slot table of 0x60-byte member rows (0x5D-byte records) starting at +0x944C, scrolled up by one row with a 0x2A0-byte memmove from +0x94AC when the roster exceeds seven members, and staging the inserted record in the last slot at +0x96EC.
evidence: Insert 0x00193018 and InsertMember 0x0019317C build a 0x60-byte record (0x00192780) and copy its 0x5D bytes with std_memcpy 0x00116C10 to self + memberIndex*0x60 + 0x944C; when the party count is >7 they first memmove 0x0011CD00(self+0x944C, self+0x94AC, 0x2A0) - a one-row (0x60-byte) upward shift of the whole 7-row block - and then write the record to self+0x96EC (= 0x944C + 0x2A0, the eighth slot). BuildEntries 0x00387258 fills the same window from the save work. Size 0x974C = 0x944C + 8*0x60.

fields.name: memberRows
fields.evidence: Row table base: std_memcpy(self + i*0x60 + 0x944C, record, 0x5D) writes member row i (stride 0x60, 0x5D-byte record built by 0x00192780 with a 7-char name at +0x4E); 0x944C..0x96EB holds rows 0..6.

fields.name: memberRowScrollSource
fields.evidence: 0x94AC = memberRows + 0x60 (row 1): std_memmove 0x0011CD00(self+0x944C, self+0x94AC, 0x2A0) copies rows 1..7 down into rows 0..6, i.e. scrolls the roster up by one row.

fields.name: memberRowLast
fields.evidence: 0x96EC = memberRows + 0x2A0 (row 7, the last of the eight 0x60-byte slots): after the scroll, std_memcpy(self+0x96EC, record, 0x5D) stores the newly inserted member record there (both Insert paths).

summary: Resource-backed layout element list: resolves a resource id at +0xC into a handle and stores a count of 8-byte entries - inline at +0x34 when the count is 1, otherwise in a heap array allocated from the UI heap.
evidence: Init 0x003D4718 stores id at +0xC, resolves it with Container_BuildPointerCache 0x00633AB0 (through Ui_GetCore 0x006F229C), then for count==1 uses self+0x34 as the entry storage, else Mem_Alloc 0x0053CF14(count*8) zeroing {u32,u32} pairs; the pointer/count go through the class offset table at 0x007A7714. Dtor 0x003D47D0 releases the handle and runs Ui_LayoutElement_Dtor. Size 0x3C = inline 8-byte entry at 0x34..0x3B.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Dtor 0x003D47D0 installs DAT_003d482c (vtable 0x00769ED8, 2 slots: 0x0065D3C4 and the dtor itself) at self[0].

fields.name: resourceId
fields.evidence: Init 0x003D4718: *(u32*)(self+0xC) = param_2, then Container_BuildPointerCache(core, param_2, param_3) resolves that id into the layout-element handle stored through the offset table.

fields.name: inlineEntries
fields.evidence: When count == 1 Init uses 'iVar3 = param_1 + 0x34' as the entry array instead of a heap allocation, so the single 8-byte {u32,u32} entry lives inline at 0x34.

summary: Intrusive text-element list: Release walks the element ring at +0x84/+0x88 (elements are embedded 0x14 bytes before their list node), destroys each element and recycles it through the second container at +0x90.
evidence: Release 0x00551AEC: piVar2 = *(int**)(self+0x88); while (piVar2 != self+0x88) { piVar1 = piVar2 - 0x14; if ((char)piVar2[-0xf] != 3) return; FUN_0011FCBC(self+0x84, piVar2); if (piVar1) { (*(*piVar1))(piVar1); FUN_00556C38(self+0x90, piVar1); } piVar2 = *piVar2; } - a remove-from-list, destroy, return-to-list pattern.

fields.name: elementListBegin
fields.evidence: FUN_0011FCBC(self+0x84, node) is called with the node being unlinked while the ring head is at self+0x88, so +0x84 is the begin pointer of the intrusive element list (the list object spans 0x84..0x8B).

fields.name: elementListEnd
fields.evidence: Iteration is 'piVar2 = *(int**)(self+0x88)' and stops when piVar2 == (int*)(self+0x88): self+0x88 is the embedded sentinel/end node of the same list. Each element sits 0x14 bytes before its node (piVar2 - 0x14).

fields.name: maybe_freeElementList
fields.evidence: FUN_00556C38(self+0x90, element) is called after the element's virtual destructor, i.e. the destroyed element is linked into a second container. A free/recycle list is the plausible reading, but no allocator side was found, hence maybe_.

summary: Four-row two-column label/value list (e.g. status window rows): writes party-member names into the left/right cell panes (pane ids from +0x28) and applies one of two palette colours or a dim tint to each row depending on the fill state and the flag at +0x48.
evidence: Init 0x004B77AC is a base-ctor + 'null_txt' initialiser that formats four left and four right cells via vtable +0x34. AddMemberRow 0x004B76F8 stores a member index into the first free byte of the four-byte array at +0x49, resolves the member with Party_Member 0x0035EB98 and writes member+0xCA (the 7-wchar name) into pane i + u16(self+0x28)<<16, then calls ApplyRowColours. ApplyRowColours 0x004B7500 reads the flag at +0x48: empty cells get palette colour 2 or 0, filled cells get the fetched colour optionally scaled by DAT_004b7688, then Ui_TextLayer_SetText 0x001A629C is called for the left and (pane|4) right cell.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: vtable 0x00776ED4 (10 slots; slot 1 Ui_Object_DtorTrivialK, slot 7 Ui_TwoColumnValueList_SetVisible, slot 8 Ui_TwoColumnValueList_Init) is the class vtable; the ctor only reaches it through the base ctor drN, so struct_db had no self[0] store.

fields.name: maybe_paneGroupId
fields.evidence: Every pane id in AddMemberRow/ApplyRowColours is 'i + (u32)*(u16*)(self+0x28)<<16' for the left cell and '(*(u16*)(self+0x28)<<16 | 4) + i' for the right cell; the exact meaning (text layer / pane group id) is not proven.

fields.name: maybe_isDimmed
fields.evidence: ApplyRowColours: cVar1 = *(char*)(self+0x48). Empty rows use palette entry 2 when cVar1==0 and entry 0 otherwise; filled rows have their colour channels scaled by DAT_004b7688 only when cVar1==0. It selects a dim/tint palette mode for the whole list; the exact meaning is not proven.

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: No real access: 0xD0 = 4 * vtable slot 0x34 from '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))' (set-text slot) in Init/AddMemberRow.

summary: Generic window that owns an embedded row table at +0x54 with a 0x3C-entry, 8-byte row array at +0x70 (0x250-byte object); only the constructor was recovered.
evidence: Ctor 0x0041D760 chains Ui_Object_CtorSmallB 0x002CFACC, installs DAT_0041d7e4 at self[0], builds the embedded row table via 0x00622248(self+0x54) (vtable LAB_0041d7e8, default 8 at table+0x18) and constructs the 0x3C x 8-byte row array at table+0x1C (= self+0x70) with std_ConstructArray 0x00100050.
